rule.manualCheck: Confirm that each of the two electives is an approved HRJ elective, is 3 credits, is at the 200-400 level, and was taken after HRJ 204 and after the minor was declared.
rule.text: Two approved, 3-credit electives that explore diverse perspectives of human rights application in professional and daily life. Examples of approved alignment include AFS 340, POL 310, and EST 325. Elective selection occurs after completion of HRJ 204; courses taken before declaring the minor are generally not applicable.
rule.reason: The page does not list the full pool of approved electives; the examples given are not an exhaustive list, so the pool cannot be expressed as a choose selector.

requirements.sourceText: 3. Interdisciplinary Electives (6 credits) - Students select two approved, 3-credit electives that explore diverse perspectives of human rights application in professional and daily life. - Major Alignment: Students are strongly encouraged to select electives from within their major department to explore the intersection of their primary field and human rights. Examples of approved alignment include: AFS 340: Human Rights in Africa, POL 310: Immigration and Refugee Policy, or EST 325: Technology in the Workplace. - Intentionality of Study: Elective selection is an intentional process occurring after the completion of HRJ 204. Consequently, courses taken prior to declaring the minor are generally not applicable to the elective requirement, ensuring that students apply the foundational theories of HRJ 204 to their subsequent elective choices.

rule.text: Completion of the minor requires 19 credits. All courses must be at the 200-400 level.

requirements.sourceText: Completion of the minor requires 19 credits. As an SBU-administered program, all 19 credits must be earned in residence at Stony Brook University. All courses must be at the 200-400 level and passed with a letter grade of C or higher.

All courses must be at the 200-400 level and passed with a letter grade of C or higher.
Completion of the minor requires 19 credits. As an SBU-administered program, all 19 credits must be earned in residence at Stony Brook University.

notes.text: Students admitted into the Social Work (BSW) major are not eligible to declare the Human Rights & Justice minor.

Students are strongly encouraged to declare the minor as early as possible, and no later than the start of their junior year. Students should consult the HRJ Program Director or Undergraduate Advisor and complete the Major/Minor Declaration Form via the Registrar's website.

HRJ 204 is the mandatory entry prerequisite for all other HRJ courses in the minor. Electives taken before completing HRJ 204 or before formally declaring the minor will not be applied toward the 19-credit requirement.
No transfer credits or retroactive credits are accepted for the minor.
All HRJ Core courses (HRJ 204, 248, 301, 310) are designed to fulfill various Stony Brook Curriculum (SBC) requirements. The page does not specify which SBC categories each course fulfills.
